title: Electromyography and nerve conduction studies

steps.tx: **Demyelinating neuropathies** in electrodiagnostic studies are characterized by marked reduction in **conduction velocity** greater than **30%** below normal, prolonged distal motor latencies exceeding **130%** of normal, and temporal dispersion or partial conduction block across non-entrapment peripheral nerve segments throughout clinical neurophysiology laboratories.
steps.say: Demyelinating neuropathies in electrodiagnostic studies are characterized by marked reduction in conduction velocity greater than 30% below normal prolonged distal motor latencies exceeding 130% of normal and temporal dispersion or partial conduction block across non-entrapment peripheral nerve segments throughout clinical neurophysiology laboratories.

left.title: Demyelinating Neuropathy
points: Conduction velocity slowed >30% below lower limit
Distal motor latencies prolonged >130% of normal
Temporal dispersion and conduction block
Relatively preserved CMAP amplitudes early

right.title: Axonal Neuropathy
points: Profound reduction of CMAP and SNAP amplitudes
Preserved or mildly slowed conduction velocity
Normal or minimally prolonged distal latencies
Prominent active denervation on needle EMG

steps.tx: The traces contrast a crisp normal motor response with a diseased study showing late onset, tiny spread out potentials. This is **demyelinating neuropathy** with prolonged distal latency, slowed **conduction velocity** and **temporal dispersion**. Conduction block across non entrapment segments helps separate it from axonal loss where amplitudes fall but speed is largely preserved.
steps.say: The traces contrast a crisp normal motor response with a diseased study showing late onset and spread out potentials. This is demyelinating neuropathy with prolonged distal latency, slowed conduction speed and temporal dispersion. Block across segments without entrapment helps separate it from axonal loss where amplitudes fall but speed is largely preserved.

vis.alt: Paired motor traces compare a normal response with prolonged latency, slowed conduction and dispersed potentials.
vis.caption: Normal and demyelinating motor responses compared, Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Axonal neuropathies** predominantly feature reduced compound muscle **action potential** and sensory nerve action potential amplitudes with relatively preserved conduction velocities and distal latencies. The primary loss of functioning axons diminishes voltage generator quantity without impairing the speed of saltatory conduction in remaining healthy myelinated fibers.
steps.say: Axonal neuropathies predominantly feature reduced compound muscle action potential and sensory nerve action potential amplitudes with relatively preserved conduction velocities and distal latencies. The primary loss of functioning axons diminishes voltage generator quantity without impairing the speed of saltatory conduction in remaining healthy myelinated fibers.

left.title: Axonal Pathophysiology
points: Loss of structural axonal cylinders
Drop in CMAP amplitude proportional to axonal loss
Drop in SNAP amplitude in sensory fibers
Velocity preserved in surviving large fibers

right.title: Diagnostic Implications
points: Seen in diabetic, toxic, and vasculitic neuropathies
Wallerian degeneration follows axonal breakdown
Fibrillations appear 2-3 weeks post injury
Collateral reinnervation produces giant MUAPs

steps.tx: Spontaneous fibrillations and **positive sharp waves** on needle electromyography represent active skeletal muscle fiber **denervation**, appearing **2** to **3** weeks after acute motor axon transection or severe axonal injury. Denervated muscle membranes express supersensitive acetylcholine receptors that undergo spontaneous rhythmic depolarization.
steps.say: Spontaneous fibrillations and positive sharp waves on needle electromyography represent active skeletal muscle fiber denervation appearing 2 to 3 weeks after acute motor axon transection or severe axonal injury. Denervated muscle membranes express supersensitive acetylcholine receptors that undergo spontaneous rhythmic depolarization.

rows: Rapid positive deflection followed by slow decay
Active muscle denervation or membrane instability
Motor neuron disease or benign irritation

steps.tx: **Fasciculation potentials** represent spontaneous motor unit discharges that occur in neurogenic disorders like **amyotrophic lateral sclerosis** as well as benign fasciculation syndrome. In motor neuron disease, widespread fasciculations in multiple body segments coexist with active fibrillations and chronic neurogenic motor unit remodeling.
steps.say: Fasciculation potentials represent spontaneous motor unit discharges that occur in neurogenic disorders like amyotrophic lateral sclerosis as well as benign fasciculation syndrome. In motor neuron disease widespread fasciculations in multiple body segments coexist with active fibrillations and chronic neurogenic motor unit remodeling.

left.title: MND / ALS Fasciculations
points: Coexist with fibrillations and positive sharp waves
Widespread in bulbar, cervical, thoracic, lumbosacral
Complex unstable polyphasic morphology
Accompanied by progressive muscle weakness and wasting

right.title: Benign Fasciculations
points: Absence of active fibrillations or sharp waves
Normal motor unit action potential morphology
Normal muscle power and deep tendon reflexes
Frequently aggravated by caffeine, stress, and fatigue

steps.tx: **Myopathic** needle electromyography demonstrates small-amplitude, short-duration, polyphasic motor unit action potentials accompanied by rapid, **early recruitment** despite weak effort. Because individual muscle fibers within the motor unit are diseased or atrophic, many units must be recruited early to generate minimal mechanical force.
steps.say: Myopathic needle electromyography demonstrates small-amplitude short-duration polyphasic motor unit action potentials accompanied by rapid early recruitment despite weak effort. Because individual muscle fibers within the motor unit are diseased or atrophic many units must be recruited early to generate minimal mechanical force.

rows: Distinguishes axonal loss from primary myopathy
Confirms motor unit remodeling versus fibre loss
Early full recruitment with low force

steps.tx: Neurogenic motor units in chronic **reinnervation** are characterized by enlarged, long-duration, **polyphasic** motor unit action potentials with reduced recruitment firing at high frequencies. Surviving motor axons sprout collateral terminals to reinnervate orphaned muscle fibers, expanding the territory and fiber density of the motor unit.
steps.say: Neurogenic motor units in chronic reinnervation are characterized by enlarged long-duration polyphasic motor unit action potentials with reduced recruitment firing at high frequencies. Surviving motor axons sprout collateral terminals to reinnervate orphaned muscle fibers expanding the territory and fiber density of the motor unit.

left.title: Collateral Sprouting
points: Terminal axonal sprouting from surviving motoneurons
Reinnervation of orphaned denervated muscle fibres
Fiber type grouping on histochemical biopsy
Synchronous firing of enlarged grouped motor units

right.title: Giant MUAP Characteristics
points: Markedly expanded duration exceeding 15 to 20 ms
Giant amplitudes often exceeding 5 to 10 mV
High polyphasic turn complexity and instability
Reduced recruitment with rapid solitary unit firing

steps.tx: **Myotonic discharges** on needle electromyography produce a characteristic waxing and waning high-frequency audio pattern resembling a **dive-bomber**, seen in myotonic dystrophy and myotonia congenita. These discharges originate from intrinsic muscle membrane hyperexcitability and delayed sarcolemmal repolarization caused by chloride or sodium channel mutations.
steps.say: Myotonic discharges on needle electromyography produce a characteristic waxing and waning high-frequency audio pattern resembling a dive-bomber seen in myotonic dystrophy and myotonia congenita. These discharges originate from intrinsic muscle membrane hyperexcitability and delayed sarcolemmal repolarization caused by chloride or sodium channel mutations.

left.title: Acoustic & Electrical Features
points: Classic dive-bomber sound on audio monitor
Spontaneous or needle insertion induced
Waxing and waning frequency (20 to 150 Hz)
Waxing and waning amplitude (10 to 1000 uV)

right.title: Clinical Channelopathies
points: Myotonic dystrophy types 1 (DMPK) and 2 (CNBP)
Myotonia congenita (CLCN1 chloride channel)
Paramyotonia congenita (SCN4A sodium channel)
Acid maltase deficiency (Pompe disease)

steps.tx: **Repetitive nerve stimulation** at low frequencies between **2** and **3** Hz demonstrates a decremental compound muscle action potential response exceeding **10%** in postsynaptic **myasthenia gravis**. Progressive depletion of readily releasable acetylcholine quanta from presynaptic terminals against blocked receptors drops endplate potentials below the threshold for muscle fiber activation.
steps.say: Repetitive nerve stimulation at low frequencies between 2 and 3 Hz demonstrates a decremental compound muscle action potential response exceeding 10% in postsynaptic myasthenia gravis. Progressive depletion of readily releasable acetylcholine quanta from presynaptic terminals against blocked receptors drops endplate potentials below the threshold for muscle fiber activation.
